speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand the underlying cause, please describe your specific physical features and any family history of similar conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency). The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth, virilization in the mother and child (hirsutism, acne, clitoromegaly), and bone fragility is highly suggestive of this condition, possibly with an associated skeletal anomaly like osteopetrosis or severe vitamin D deficiency. I will confirm with an electrolyte panel and 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels.
